symbols.name: B_\pi
symbols.def: \(B_\pi(u,v)=u e_b e_a^{\mathsf T}+v e_c e_b^{\mathsf T}\)

symbols.name: \ell_{23}^{\mathrm{M2}}
symbols.def: the retained released-code variable, identified by \(\ell_{23}^{\mathrm{M2}}=\beta\)

symbols.name: L_{\mathrm{pub}}
symbols.def: \(L_{\mathrm{pub}}=\begin{pmatrix}1&-\gamma_1&-\gamma_2&-\gamma_3\\0&1&-u&0\\0&0&1&-\beta\\0&0&0&1\end{pmatrix}\), the upper-triangular residual transformation with negative edge entries in the released row-vector convention

symbols.name: \Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}}
symbols.def: the observed-row block of \(L_{\mathrm{pub}}^{-\mathsf T}\), namely \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}}=\begin{pmatrix}\gamma_1&1&0&0\\u\gamma_1+\gamma_2&u&1&0\\\beta(u\gamma_1+\gamma_2)+\gamma_3&\beta u&\beta&1\end{pmatrix}\), with rows indexed by observed nodes \(1,2,3\) and columns indexed by sources \(0,1,2,3\)

symbols.name: \vartheta_{\mathbb R}
symbols.role: parameters of the fixed published one-proxy graph through order three

symbols.name: \widetilde\Phi_{\le3}
symbols.def: \(\widetilde\Phi_{\le3}(\vartheta_{\mathbb R})=(\beta,\mathbf m)\) with \(m_{ik}=\sum_{j=0}^3\omega_j^{(2)}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}})_{ij}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}})_{kj}\) for \(1\le i\le k\le3\), and \(c_{ik\ell}=\sum_{j=0}^3\omega_j^{(3)}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}})_{ij}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}})_{kj}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}})_{\ell j}\) for \(1\le i\le k\le\ell\le3\)

symbols.name: \mathcal G_{\mathrm{pin}}
symbols.def: the entire \(110\)-column Groebner basis of \(\mathcal I_{\le3}\) produced over \(\mathbb Q\), with lexicographic order on \(\ell_{23}^{\mathrm{M2}}=\beta\) followed by the six second-moment and ten third-moment coordinates, by \(\texttt{Macaulay2/NonGaussianIdentifiability.m2}\) at commit \(\texttt{ff808aff1a458a4ccba7a54ff56bf139ab03471f}\) for four nodes, cumulant order \(3\), edges \(\{(0,1),(0,2),(0,3),(1,2),(2,3)\}\), and hidden-node cutoff \(0\)

symbols.name: \mathcal I_{\le3}^{(W)}
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I_{\le3}^{(W)}=S_W^{-1}\mathcal I_{\le3}\subset S_W^{-1}\mathbb F[\beta,\mathbf m]\); equivalently its contraction is \(\mathcal I_{\le3}:(W_2^{\mathrm{el}})^\infty\)

novel.justification: This sign-and-margin chamber represents reinforcing propagation and a common positive latent shock, as in monotone production, demand, and biological signaling chains; it is stated as the substantive semialgebraic restriction whose identifying content is characterized.
The normalization permits heterogeneous idiosyncratic scales around the latent-source variance benchmark and describes a compact calibration class rather than an oracle restriction.
A common skew direction arises for centered bounded arrival, demand, and shock variables; the interval permits unequal source laws and rules out only weak or sign-canceling skewness.

definitions.name: \mathcal P_+
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal P_+=\{P:\exists(\pi,u,v,\gamma,s,H,\xi)\text{ satisfying }X=A_\pi(\gamma H+\operatorname{diag}(s)\xi),\ H\perp\!\!\!\perp\xi_1\perp\!\!\!\perp\xi_2\perp\!\!\!\perp\xi_3,\ \mathbb E[(H,\xi^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}]=0_4,\ \operatorname{diag}\operatorname{Cov}((H,\xi^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T})=\mathbf1_4,\ \mathbb P((H,\xi^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\in[-2,2]^4)=1,\ (u,v,\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_3)\in[1/4,3/4]^5,\ s\in[3/4,5/4]^3,\ \kappa\in[1/2,1]^4\}\]

definitions.name: \operatorname{Rec}
definitions.construction: \[a=\operatorname*{arg\,unique}_{i\in\mathcal V}\{\operatorname{rank}(M_i)=2\},\quad \widetilde k\in\ker(M_a)\setminus\{0\},\quad b=\operatorname*{arg\,unique}_{j\ne a}\{\operatorname{sgn}(\widetilde k_j)=-\operatorname{sgn}(\widetilde k_a)\},\quad c=\mathcal V\setminus\{a,b\},\quad N=\operatorname{adj}(M_a)e_c,\quad W=M_bN,\quad \operatorname{Rec}(C)=B_\pi\!\left(-\frac{N_aW_b}{D},\frac{W_c}{W_b}\right)\]

definitions.name: \Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}}
definitions.construction: For the exact graph with latent node \(0\), observed nodes \(1,2,3\), and edges \(0\to1\), \(0\to2\), \(0\to3\), \(1\to2\), and \(2\to3\), use the released row-vector residual transform \[L_{\mathrm{pub}}=\begin{pmatrix}1&-\gamma_1&-\gamma_2&-\gamma_3\\0&1&-u&0\\0&0&1&-\beta\\0&0&0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad \Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}}=\begin{pmatrix}\gamma_1&1&0&0\\u\gamma_1+\gamma_2&u&1&0\\\beta(u\gamma_1+\gamma_2)+\gamma_3&\beta u&\beta&1\end{pmatrix}.\] The latter is the observed-row block of \(L_{\mathrm{pub}}^{-\mathsf T}\). Define \(m_{ik}=\sum_{j=0}^3\omega_j^{(2)}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}})_{ij}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}})_{kj}\) and \(c_{ik\ell}=\sum_{j=0}^3\omega_j^{(3)}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}})_{ij}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}})_{kj}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}})_{\ell j}\). The retained coordinates are exactly \(\mathbf m^{(2)}=(m_{11},m_{12},m_{13},m_{22},m_{23},m_{33})\) and \(\mathbf c=(c_{111},c_{112},c_{113},c_{122},c_{123},c_{133},c_{222},c_{223},c_{233},c_{333})\).

definitions.name: \mathcal J_{\le3}
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal J_{\le3}=\left\langle m_{ik}-\sum_{j=0}^3\omega_j^{(2)}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}})_{ij}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}})_{kj}:1\le i\le k\le3\right\rangle+\left\langle c_{ik\ell}-\sum_{j=0}^3\omega_j^{(3)}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}})_{ij}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}})_{kj}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}})_{\ell j}:1\le i\le k\le\ell\le3\right\rangle\subset\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pub}}.\] This is the parameterized form of the released residual-diagonal covariance equations and off-diagonal cubic residual equations over \(\mathbb F=\mathbb Q\).

definitions.name: \mathcal I_{\le3}
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal I_{\le3}=\mathcal J_{\le3}\cap\mathbb F[\beta,\mathbf m],\qquad \mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}=\mathcal I_{\le3}\cap\mathbb F[\mathbf m],\qquad K_{\mathrm{obs}}=\operatorname{Frac}(\mathbb F[\mathbf m]/\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}).\] Thus \(\mathcal I_{\le3}\) eliminates \(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_3,u,\omega^{(2)},\omega^{(3)}\) while retaining the published effect \(\beta\) and all sixteen observed moment coordinates.

definitions.name: \mathcal I_{\le3}^{(W)}
definitions.construction: \[S_W=\{(W_2^{\mathrm{el}})^k:k\in\mathbb N_0\},\qquad \mathcal I_{\le3}^{(W)}=S_W^{-1}\mathcal I_{\le3}\subset S_W^{-1}\mathbb F[\beta,\mathbf m].\] Localization therefore means inversion of the single observable polynomial \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\); its contraction to \(\mathbb F[\beta,\mathbf m]\) is the saturation \(\mathcal I_{\le3}:(W_2^{\mathrm{el}})^\infty\). Extension afterward to \(K_{\mathrm{obs}}[\beta]\) inverts every nonzero observable class.

definitions.name: \mathfrak A
definitions.construction: Apply chartwise saturation of the full covariance-and-cubic moment ideal by every nonzero \(2\times2\) slice minor and every adjugate contraction denominator, then perform real primary decomposition and solve the six order-specific fibers on each sign cell.

statements.statement: For every \(\kappa_0\in[1/2,1]\), let \(b_0=(\kappa_0+\sqrt{\kappa_0^2+4})/2\) and \(a_0=1/b_0\). The two-point law placing probabilities \(b_0/(a_0+b_0)\) and \(a_0/(a_0+b_0)\) on \(-a_0\) and \(b_0\), respectively, is centered, has variance one, support in \([-2,2]\), and third cumulant \(\kappa_0\). Independent products of four such laws make \(\mathcal P_+\) nonempty for every \(\kappa\in[1/2,1]^4\).
statements.justification: This prevents the compact skewness and support restrictions from describing an empty or moment-incompatible model.
statements.gap: The cited LiNGAM papers normalize source moments but do not verify simultaneous bounded-support realizability for the entire maintained skewness interval.
statements.consumer: The finite-sample inversion theorem uses this result to interpret every retained moment parameter as an attainable source law.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_+\) with \(\pi=(a,b,c)\), the tensor in causal coordinates satisfies \[C=hg^{\otimes3}+rd^{\otimes3}+te^{\otimes3}+wf^{\otimes3}.\] Its slices obey \[M_a=hxgg^{\mathsf T}+rdd^{\mathsf T},\qquad \ker(M_a)=\operatorname{span}\{k\},\] and \[\det(M_b)=hrtu p z^2,\qquad \det(M_c)=hrtu v^2qz^2+hrwuvqy^2+htwvqx^2+rtwuv^2.\]
statements.justification: The factorization exposes both the unique low-rank root slice and the contractions that isolate the two directed coefficients.
statements.gap: Cai et al. (2023) factor a one-latent block and Schkoda, Robeva, and Drton (2024) stack several cumulant orders; neither records this joint cubic chain factorization and its three slice determinants.
statements.consumer: The rank, sign, denominator, and perturbation arguments all reduce to these identities.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_+\), exactly one slice \(M_i\) has rank two, and its label is \(a\); the other two slices have rank three. Every nonzero \(\widetilde k\in\ker(M_a)\) has nonzero coordinates, and \(b\) is the unique label whose coordinate has sign opposite to \(\widetilde k_a\). With \(c=\mathcal V\setminus\{a,b\}\), \(N=\operatorname{adj}(M_a)e_c\), and \(W=M_bN\), \[v=\frac{W_c}{W_b},\qquad u=-\frac{N_aW_b}{N_bW_b+N_cW_c},\qquad \operatorname{Rec}(C)=B_\pi(u,v).\] Uniformly on \(\mathcal P_+\), \[|W_b|\ge d_W,\qquad |D|\ge d_D,\qquad |\det(M_b)|\ge d_b,\qquad |\det(M_c)|\ge d_c.\] Thus \(C_3(P)\) globally identifies the labeled chain and both direct coefficients, and \(\operatorname{Rec}\) has constant arithmetic cost.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: skewness alone recovers the unknown mechanism globally rather than selecting among algebraic candidates.
statements.gap: Tramontano et al. (2025), Theorem 3.6, reports nonidentification through order three on the fixed unrestricted graph; Cai et al. (2023) does not recover this unknown six-chain structure from \(C_3\) alone.
statements.consumer: CEId-from-Moments can replace its fourth-cumulant one-proxy initializer by a certified cubic branch on the positive-skew chamber.

statements.statement: Identify the retained released variable by \(\ell_{23}^{\mathrm{M2}}=\beta\), the released coordinates \(s_{ij}=m_{ij}\) for \(1\le i\le j\le3\), and \(t_{ijk}=c_{ijk}\) for \(1\le i\le j\le k\le3\). For the exact pinned computation defining \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{pin}}\), division of \(R_{\mathrm{el}}=\beta W_2^{\mathrm{el}}-W_3^{\mathrm{el}}\) by the entire basis \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{pin}}\) has zero remainder.
statements.justification: The pinned zero remainder is the reproducible gate connecting the independently derived linear relation to the exact released full elimination basis.
statements.gap: Tramontano et al. (2025), Theorem 3.6 and its released Macaulay2 file, report the retained elimination output but do not report the normal form of this additional linear relation against the entire basis.
statements.consumer: The localized degree calculation proceeds only if this exact-arithmetic checkpoint succeeds; a nonzero remainder terminates the re-audit claim.

statements.statement: For the exact published one-proxy map \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}}\), the class of \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\) is nonzero in \(\mathbb F[\mathbf m]/\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}\), and the additional relation \(R_{\mathrm{el}}=\beta W_2^{\mathrm{el}}-W_3^{\mathrm{el}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal I_{\le3}\). In the stated localization, \(\beta-W_3^{\mathrm{el}}/W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\in\mathcal I_{\le3}^{(W)}\); after quotienting by the localized observable ideal and extending to the observable function field, \[\mathcal I_{\le3}K_{\mathrm{obs}}[\beta]=\left\langle\beta-\frac{W_3^{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}\right\rangle.\] Therefore the generic full covariance-and-cubic fiber of \(\beta\) has degree one on \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\ne0\). Once the pinned checkpoint is established, this is a strict generic tightening of the nonidentification conclusion in Tramontano et al. (2025), Theorem 3.6, on the same parameterized moment map.
statements.justification: The theorem turns an independently derived cubic contraction into a precisely testable statement about the exact released full ideal and its observable localization.
statements.gap: Tramontano et al. (2025), Theorem 3.6, reports generic nonidentification through order three; the unreported object tested here is the localized full-ideal relation \(\beta W_2^{\mathrm{el}}-W_3^{\mathrm{el}}=0\) under the exact published parameterization.
statements.consumer: The result determines whether the one-proxy implementation may use a generic cubic effect chart on \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\ne0\), subject to the pinned replication gate.

statements.statement: Let \(\pi_f=(1,2,3)\) and \(\pi_r=(3,2,1)\), and fix \(u=v=3/10\). For \(\pi_f\), take \(\gamma=(7/10,2/5,43027/61000)\) and \(s^2=(13/10,4/5,341693977/372100000)\); reverse the coordinates for \(\pi_r\). Both parameter points are interior to their positive boxes, \[\Psi_{\pi_f}(3/10,3/10,\gamma,s)=\Psi_{\pi_r}(3/10,3/10,\gamma^{\mathrm{rev}},s^{\mathrm{rev}})=\Sigma_0,\] and both six-by-six Jacobians of \((\gamma,s^2)\mapsto\Psi_\pi(3/10,3/10,\gamma,s)\) have nonzero determinant at these points. Therefore \(\Sigma_0\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal S_{\pi_f}\cap\mathcal S_{\pi_r})\), so covariance alone fails to identify the order on a nonempty open set.
statements.justification: An open overlap proves that the cubic tensor, rather than covariance information already implicit in the model, performs the order identification.
statements.gap: Ghassami et al. (2020) characterize distribution equivalence abstractly, while Foygel Barber et al. (2022) treat known-graph covariance recovery; neither gives this pairwise positive-chain image overlap.
statements.consumer: The overlap supplies a rigorous ablation benchmark for any implementation claiming that the chain label is learned from skewness.

statements.statement: For every \(n\ge1\) and \(0<\alpha<1\), \[\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_+}\mathbb P_P\!\left(B_\pi(u,v)\in\mathsf{CS}_n(\alpha)\right)\ge1-\alpha.\] If \(2\varepsilon_n(\alpha)<\delta_0\), then on \(\{\|\widehat C-C\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_n(\alpha)\}\), every element of \(\mathsf{CS}_n(\alpha)\) has the true label and \[\operatorname{diam}_\infty(\mathsf{CS}_n(\alpha))\le2L_\star\varepsilon_n(\alpha)=O(n^{-1/2}).\] These conclusions hold for every rank of \(\operatorname{Var}_P(\operatorname{vech}(X^{\otimes3}))\).
statements.justification: The set gives honest uncertainty quantification across discrete order selection and rational denominators without a Wald approximation.
statements.gap: Tramontano et al. (2025) provide point estimators but no coverage theorem; Babii (2020) and Andrews and Guggenberger (2019) do not treat a finite union of exact LvLiNGAM charts.
statements.consumer: CEId-from-Moments can return a certified effect set and an order-ambiguity warning even when empirical moment covariance is singular.

statements.statement: As a direct target-compatibility corollary, on the fixed order \(\pi=(1,2,3)\), \(\operatorname{Rec}(C)=B_\pi(u,v)\) returns \(v=B_{\pi,32}\). For the same \(P\in\mathcal P_+\), the causal effect identified in Tramontano et al. (2025), Theorem 3.5, is defined as this same structural coordinate.
statements.justification: This bookkeeping corollary records target compatibility and requires no independent fourth-order root solve.
statements.gap: The published fourth-order result and the cubic inverse use different information, so their common structural coordinate must be stated without treating equality of targets as a new identification theorem.
statements.consumer: The compatibility remark preserves the treatment-to-outcome interpretation when the cubic chart is used in the published workflow.

statements.statement: Construct \(\mathfrak A\) so that the unrestricted real parameter space of every \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_3\) is partitioned into finitely many semialgebraic strata on each of which the fiber of \(\widetilde\Phi_{\le3}\) has a certified constant cardinality and a certified set of chain orders. For every singleton-order stratum, provide an observable rational chart for \(u\) and \(v\); for every non-singleton or positive-dimensional stratum, provide explicit real parameter twins or a fiber parameterization. Determine on all intersections of rank-drop and denominator-zero hypersurfaces whether the failure of \(\operatorname{Rec}\) is removable or is genuine nonidentification.
statements.justification: This exposes the genuine unresolved content instead of equating one failed rational denominator with structural ambiguity.
statements.gap: Generic elimination in Tramontano et al. (2025) and Garcia-Puente et al. (2010) does not classify real fibers on exceptional intersections; Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant (2011) do not cover this higher-moment latent LiNGAM map.
statements.consumer: A completed atlas yields exact ambiguity warnings and alternate formulas for observations near every failure divisor of the cubic branch.

sampling_model.design: Independent observational sampling from one unknown law \(P\in\mathcal P_+\).
sampling_model.units: The observations \(X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(n)}\) are identically distributed three-vectors.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no assigned treatment; the directed coefficients \(u\) and \(v\) are structural causal effects in the labeled chain.
sampling_model.overlap: The six discrete chain labels are all admissible, and the positive coefficient, loading, scale, and skewness boxes supply uniform algebraic separation.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The confidence set inverts all ten empirical cubic coordinates jointly; it does not estimate or invert their influence covariance.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The causal effect from \(T\) to \(Y\) is not identifiable from the first three cumulants.
Theorem 3.5 identifies the proxy-graph effect using cumulants through the fourth order.
Theorem 2 gives a closed-form one-latent-component loading recovery using covariance and fourth cumulants.
The source-rank theorem uses stacked cumulant orders and generic rank distinctions to recover source direction.
Propositions 2--4 characterize identifiability through the elimination ideal of a modified polynomial parameterization.
Distribution equivalence compares directed structures through equality or generic overlap of their observational model images.
Concentration inequalities yield honest confidence sets and diameter control for ill-posed inverse problems.
Singularity-robust test inversion permits nonlinear moment inference when the moment covariance matrix is singular.

tldr: A positive-skew, one-global-confounder three-node chain is globally invertible from its third cumulant tensor alone. The unique rank-two slice locates the root, its signed kernel locates the middle node, and two adjugate contractions recover both edges with uniform denominator margins. On the exact published proxy graph, an independent full-ideal replication and re-audit tests the additional localized relation \(\beta W_2^{\mathrm{el}}-W_3^{\mathrm{el}}=0\), with zero remainder against the pinned entire basis as the first checkpoint; a complete real exceptional-fiber atlas remains an explicit open question. An opposite-chain covariance overlap proves that skewness supplies genuinely new order information, while simultaneous bounded-moment inversion gives finite-sample uniform coverage and root-\(n\) diameter without nonsingular influence covariance.

project_justification.gap: The closest proxy-LvLiNGAM result uses fourth-order cumulants for identification and reports nonidentification through order three on the exact one-proxy graph. The status of the independently derived localized relation \(\beta W_2^{\mathrm{el}}-W_3^{\mathrm{el}}=0\) under the released full elimination basis is not reported, and existing cumulant rank methods neither resolve the compact positive chamber nor classify real failures of rational charts.
project_justification.niche: The joint three-variable cubic tensor has chain-specific rank and sign geometry that is invisible to bivariate root enumeration and can collapse both label and coefficient ambiguity.
project_justification.fill: The project derives a constant-cost rational recovery map with global positive-chamber margins, independently replicates and re-audits the exact published full ideal with a pinned zero-remainder gate, proves a covariance-only open overlap, attaches honest finite-sample inversion, and isolates complete real-fiber stratification as the first-class unresolved theorem question.

related_work: Tramontano et al. (2025), Theorems 3.5--3.6, Figure 3, Appendix C.1.1, and the released \(\texttt{NonGaussianIdentifiability.m2}\) file provide the exact one-proxy graph, the fourth-order estimator, and the reported third-order boundary. The localized theorem is an independent full-ideal replication and re-audit of that boundary: it tests the specifically alleged additional relation \(\beta W_2^{\mathrm{el}}-W_3^{\mathrm{el}}=0\) and does not attribute a restricted proof strategy to the published argument. Cai et al. (2023), Theorem 2 and Appendix A.1, motivate closed-form cumulant extraction for a one-latent component but use covariance with a selected higher order. Schkoda, Robeva, and Drton (2024), their source-rank theorem, motivate the rank diagnostic but stack orders three and four for one latent parent. Garcia-Puente, Spielvogel, and Sullivant (2010), Propositions 2--4, supply the full-elimination-ideal criterion used in the independent re-audit. Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant (2011) supply the global-versus-generic fiber distinction used to formulate the exceptional atlas. Ghassami et al. (2020) motivate comparison of entire model images, while Foygel Barber et al. (2022) treat rational covariance recovery for known explicit-latent graphs rather than cross-label overlap. Babii (2020) and Andrews and Guggenberger (2019) inform the confidence-set inversion, but neither treats exact bounded cubic charts with discrete causal-order selection.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact released graph, the \(3\times4\) mixing convention, all six covariance coordinates, all ten cubic coordinates, and the proposed linear relation are specified in the formal core. The pinned Macaulay2 run has not yet printed the entire stored basis reduction of \(R_{\mathrm{el}}\) or the localized target degree. Zero remainder against that full basis is the first proof checkpoint: a nonzero remainder or a retained generic second full-system root ends the localized re-audit claim. Until this checkpoint succeeds, the independent symbolic derivation does not supersede the conclusion of Theorem 3.6. The unrestricted real atlas is also not claimed: known zero-skew twins and removable zero-column chart failures show that a denominator divisor alone cannot equal the nonidentification locus.
honest_scope: The theorem targets concern global recovery on the compact positive chamber, a pinned and explicitly gated full-ideal re-audit on the fixed published graph, an explicit covariance-overlap neighborhood, and exact moment-set coverage. The localized degree-one target stands only if the full-basis zero-remainder checkpoint succeeds. The complete classification of all real fibers outside the chamber remains open. As a sanity reduction, on the fixed order \(1\to2\to3\) the cubic functional returns the same structural \(T\to Y\) coordinate targeted by the published fourth-order functional; this is a direct compatibility corollary, not a separate root-solving result. With no latent factor the structural target reduces to ordinary fully observed LiNGAM recovery as in Shimizu et al. (2006), although the displayed latent-slice chart is then unnecessary.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Tramontano et al. (2025), Theorem 3.6; Garcia-Puente et al. (2010), Section 2; Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant (2011), global-versus-generic injectivity criterion
seed_details.live_opportunity: Neither generic elimination nor one rational chart distinguishes removable denominator failures from genuine twins on intersections of exceptional hypersurfaces.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace a single localization by saturation on every nonzero slice-minor chart, followed by real primary decomposition and fiber-cardinality certification.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for real fiber stratification of the one-proxy LvLiNGAM moment map found global-identifiability frameworks but no chart-complete semialgebraic atlas for this model.
seed_details.cynical_objection: The atlas is a routine computer-algebra appendix once the generic inverse is known.
seed_details.rebuttal: Rank-drop and denominator intersections can carry positive-dimensional fibers, finite twins, or alternate rational charts, and real feasibility is not resolved by generic degree.
seed_details.disposition: keep as the first-class open question

seed_details.seed: Finite-sample honest inversion of bounded cubic moments without covariance inversion
seed_details.anchor_locator: Tramontano et al. (2025), Section 4 and conclusion; Babii (2020), concentration-based confidence-set construction; Andrews and Guggenberger (2019), singularity-robust test inversion
seed_details.live_opportunity: The published estimator has no coverage theory, and ordinary delta-method inference is nonregular at rational failure divisors or singular moment covariance.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Invert a simultaneous bounded-moment rectangle over all six exact charts before selecting a label.
seed_details.destination_search: The target-method search found singularity-robust asymptotic GMM and honest inverse-problem sets, but no finite-sample union-of-cubic-charts result.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Coverage follows immediately from Hoeffding's inequality.
seed_details.rebuttal: Coverage is elementary, but root-\(n\) contraction requires a uniform label-separation and rational inverse-Lipschitz theorem; this is retained as an inference rung rather than the kernel.
seed_details.disposition: fold into the selected kernel as an inference rung

seed_details.seed: Open covariance overlap of opposite positive chains
seed_details.anchor_locator: Ghassami et al. (2020), Definitions 1--2 and main equivalence theorem; Foygel Barber et al. (2022), Theorem 3.7
seed_details.live_opportunity: Known-graph covariance recovery does not determine whether distinct unknown chain labels have full-dimensional covariance-image intersections.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Form the fiber product of two chain-specific covariance maps and certify an interior common value by a submersion Jacobian.
seed_details.destination_search: Pairwise covariance-image overlap searches found general distribution equivalence and fixed-graph half-trek criteria, but no positive one-factor three-chain result.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Parameter counting already implies that the covariance images overlap.
seed_details.rebuttal: Dimension counts do not establish a real feasible common interior point; an exact interior witness and two nonsingular Jacobians do.
seed_details.disposition: fold into the selected kernel as the covariance impossibility contrast

seed_details.seed: Necessary-and-sufficient signed-kernel chamber for chain-order recovery
seed_details.anchor_locator: Tramontano et al. (2025), Figure 3 and Theorem 3.6; Cai et al. (2023), causal-order corollary
seed_details.live_opportunity: The positive chamber is sufficient, but the exact real sign inequalities under which a slice kernel orients the chain are not characterized.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Solve the kernel sign inequalities \(uz(z+vy)>0\) and \(uzy>0\) jointly with slice-rank conditions before recovering edges.
seed_details.destination_search: No paper in the adjacent cumulant-order literature gives an if-and-only-if signed-kernel chamber for this three-node latent-factor model.
seed_details.cynical_objection: This is merely rewriting the coordinates of a cross product.
seed_details.rebuttal: A complete necessity direction must also construct observationally compatible order ambiguity outside the chamber; absent that, this seed is not yet a standalone kernel.
seed_details.disposition: drop as a standalone seed and absorb into the real-fiber question

seed_details.seed: Adaptive adjugate-chart atlas for rational recovery beyond positivity
seed_details.anchor_locator: Garcia-Puente et al. (2010), Example 1 and Propositions 3--4; Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant (2011), rational-identifiability analysis
seed_details.live_opportunity: A zero chosen adjugate column need not imply nonidentification because another column or kernel normalization can remain valid.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Enumerate all nonzero adjugate columns and select a chart using observable minors before forming rational contractions.
seed_details.destination_search: General rational-identifiability papers discuss exceptional sets but do not provide this model's constant-size observable chart selector.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Finite chart switching is a software detail with no theorem content.
seed_details.rebuttal: It becomes mathematical only when the chart union is proved equal to the identifiable locus; that equality is subsumed by the stronger fiber atlas.
seed_details.disposition: drop in favor of the complete atlas

seed_details.seed: Minimal cumulant-order frontier when selected source skewnesses vanish
seed_details.anchor_locator: Cai et al. (2023), Section 2 and Appendix A.1; Schkoda, Robeva, and Drton (2024), source-rank theorem and discussion
seed_details.live_opportunity: Existing procedures move to some higher nonzero cumulant when skewness vanishes, without an exact order frontier for the proxy-chain target.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the cubic slice by the first nonzero odd or even source-cumulant flattening and track which source columns remain distinguishable.
seed_details.destination_search: The adjacent papers provide sufficient orders depending on latent count but no exact source-pattern-dependent minimum for the fixed three-node proxy chain.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Choosing the next nonzero cumulant is immediate from multilinearity.
seed_details.rebuttal: Exact minimality requires lower-order twins for every vanishing pattern, but this direction is less valuable than resolving the published cubic boundary by a reproducible full-ideal re-audit.

novelty_justification: The closest published result is Tramontano et al. (2025), Theorem 3.6, which reports that the effect is not identifiable from cumulants through order three on the exact fixed graph. The independent full-ideal theorem tests a precisely specified additional relation, \(\beta W_2^{\mathrm{el}}-W_3^{\mathrm{el}}=0\), under the exact released parameterization, with zero remainder against the pinned entire basis as a mandatory first checkpoint; it makes no claim about which subset of the published computation supported Theorem 3.6. The positive-class theorem is stronger in a different direction because it recovers the unknown order and both direct coefficients globally from \(C_3\) alone with explicit denominator margins. Cai et al. (2023) and Schkoda, Robeva, and Drton (2024) supply the nearest cumulant-factorization and rank techniques, but require covariance with a fourth cumulant or stacked orders and do not deliver this recovery map. Exact-title, theorem-number, code, and target-method searches through September 14, 2026 found no closer paper or public full-basis re-audit that subsumes either theorem.
